loadCloudData.label: Load cloud data
loadCloudData.doc:
Streams a cloud document, or a collection query's documents, into variable `variable` while the screen shows: `{status: loading|loaded| error, isLoading, data, error, hasMore}`. A variable of type list gets the documents themselves, and with an `aggregate`, a number variable the number. Blocking actions wait for the first value; an initial failure stops the chain. A later subscription failure stops any remaining actions from that invocation and fires the canvas's actionError reaction. Subscriptions close on error or when the screen is disposed.

One variable has one live load: running the action again (or a `ReloadCloudDataAction`) replaces the earlier subscription. Unless `reactive` is false, the load runs again by itself when a value its query reads changes (`${auth.uid}`, `${search}`, a `limit` bound to a variable), but never for a change of its own variable.

Up to `kMaxCloudBatchWrites` writes are all or none. More are committed in chunks of that size, each all or none; with `transaction`, more fail before anything is written. A batch with a read step (get, query, count, sum, average) runs its steps one by one, as before.

One tween a `NodeAnimation` drives: a property at a binding `path` of a node, or a `variable`.

The value at the controller's value `v` (after the animation's curve): `u` is `v` inside `interval` (`Interval(begin, end)`), eased by `curve` (`CurveTween`); then `wave`s added to `from`, else the `keyframes` (`TweenSequence`), else `Tween(begin: from, end: to)` at `u`. On a replacing track a wave's amplitude is a share of the way from `from` to `to` (the property's own value when `to` is omitted): `{"from": 0, "wave": [{}]}` swings a property between its own value and as far the other way, once a run (a pendulum). InputIcon.doc: An icon an input shows (`Icon`): a glyph as the icon node's `icon` prop (`{"source", "name", "codepoint", ...}` or an image), its size and color, and the actions a tap on it runs.

Keyframe.doc: One stop of a `TweenSequence`: the track's `value` at `at` (0–1 of the track's run), reached on `curve` from the stop before it.

ListReorder.doc: Dragging a list's items to a new place, within the list and, with a `group`, into other lists of the group (a Kanban board). A drop runs the list's `reorder` reactions with `${result.from}`, `${result.to}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.fromList}` and `${result.toList}`.

fields.doc: Lists of one group take each other's items; empty: within this list.
This list in `${result.fromList}` / `${result.toList}` (an expression); empty: the list's id.
Must hold for an item (`${item}`, `${index}`) to be picked up.
Must hold for a drop (`${result}` as the drop would be).
A focused item moves with Alt and the arrow keys, and is announced.
The numeric field of a document's position (`ListApply.cloud`).
The field of the list a document is in, for moves between lists.

ListSections.doc: Groups a data list's consecutive items with the same `groupBy` value into sections, each under the list's `sectionHeader` slot.

fields.doc: A path in the item (`group`, `date.day`) or an expression.
The current section's header stays pinned until the next pushes it out.
An index of the sections' keys along the list's edge (A–Z).

The keys the index shows, in order (`A`…`Z`); empty shows the sections'. A key no item has is drawn in `indexMutedColor` and does nothing. With a data-paged list the keys of every item count, and picking one loads pages until its section is in.
The index's text (font, size, weight, color).
A key while it is touched.
A key no item has.

Measure.doc: Writes where the node is laid out, `{x, y, width, height, centerX, centerY}` in pixels, to a variable as layout changes: in the coordinates of the ancestor node `relativeTo` (empty: the screen), under `key` when the variable is a map. Other nodes then follow it: a marker travelling to the chip of the reader's layer on a timeline whose chips are laid out by data. The design canvas measures too.

fields.doc: The variable its box is written to.
The key it's written under, for a map variable.
An ancestor node whose box it's measured in; empty: the screen.

Motion.doc:
A transform painted over the node's layout (Flutter's `Transform`): it moves nothing else. Its values are the node's rest pose; how it gets there is the node's `animations` and `transitions`.

One matrix, outermost first: a translation (the `path`'s offset, then `translateX`/`translateY` in pixels, then `shiftX`/`shiftY` times the node's size, `FractionalTranslation`), then about `alignment`: the scale (`scale` times `scaleX`/`scaleY`), the rotation `rotate` (degrees, about z, plus the path's turn), then `rotateX` and `rotateY` (3D, seen with `perspective`). JSON (sparse): `{"translateY": -4, "scale": 1.02, "alignment": [0, 1]}`.

Schema 2's other motion keys (`originX`/`originY`, the flat path keys, `opacity`, `blur`, the timing, entrance, loop, spin, keyframes and shimmer) are rewritten by the schema-3 migration (`migrate2to3`).

fields.doc: Pixels.
Pixels (`Transform.translate(offset:)`).
Times the node's size (`FractionalTranslation`).
Multiples of the node's own size (`FractionalTranslation`).
The axis factors multiply `scale`.
`Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`.
`Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`.
Degrees, about z.
Degrees, in 3D.
Degrees. `rotate` turns about z (`Transform.rotate`); `rotateX` and `rotateY` turn in 3D, seen with `perspective` (0 flat).
How strongly a 3D rotation is seen in depth (0 flat).
The point scale and rotation are about (`Transform.alignment`).
Not painted while its back faces the viewer (through every transform above it too).
A path the node sits on.

NavigationDestination.doc: A navigation bar item: Flutter's `NavigationDestination` (and `BottomNavigationBarItem`). Icon colors are the item's own, over the bar's. `actions` are its reactions.

fields.doc: `BottomNavigationBarItem.backgroundColor` (shifting bars).

NodeAnimation.doc:
One `AnimationController` on a node and the tweens it drives (behavior key `animations`, a list). A screen-wide one sits on the canvas node.

Its value runs 0 → 1 over `duration` (back over `reverseDuration`), after `delay`, eased by `curve` (`CurvedAnimation`), `repeat`ed or once; on a `spring` instead of the clock; or follows `progress` (an expression) with no clock at all. Each track maps that value to its property (`AnimationTrack`).

`preset` names a short form (`pulse`, `shake`, `spin`... see `AnimationPresets`) whose tracks and timing it stands for, with `params`; fields given here override the preset's (`expanded`).

Read as `${animation.<id>.value}` (after `curve`), `.status` (`dismissed`, `forward`, `reverse`, `completed`) and `.isAnimating` by the node and the nodes inside it; driven by the `animate` action.

fields.doc: Unique on the node; what `animate` and `${animation.<id>}` name.
A short form (`AnimationPresets`); its params below.
Off, it applies nothing and doesn't run (the node shows its own values). Bindable.
Milliseconds; empty: the preset's, else 300.
`AnimationController.duration` / `reverseDuration` (ms); null: the preset's, else 300.
Waits this long (ms) before each play starts; the value holds at its start meanwhile.
Applied to the controller's value before every track; null: the preset's, else linear.
`repeat(reverse:, count:)`; null: the preset's, else plays once.
Plays when the node appears; false waits for `playKey` or an action. Null: the preset's, else true.
A change plays it from the start (bindable).
Holds the controller where it is (`stop()`) while true; it carries on when false. Held before it starts, it waits at its start. Bindable.
Where a play starts in its cycle (0–1).
Runs on this spring instead of `duration` and `curve`: `animateWith(SpringSimulation(spring, 0, 1, 0))`.
An expression giving its value (0–1) instead of a clock.
The point the scale and rotation of its adding and multiplying tracks are about (`ScaleTransition(alignment:)`); null: the preset's, else the center.
Where the design canvas draws it (a share of a cycle); empty: not applied there.
Ms to speed up from still, and to slow to a stop when paused.
Waits to start until this share of the node is in view.

NoisePaint.doc: A `noise` paint's procedural noise, parameterised as SVG's `<feTurbulence>` (`baseFrequency`, `numOctaves`, `seed`, `type`): the texture a web page's grain overlay draws (`filter: url(#grain)`), here a paint, drawn as a seamless tile repeated over the box.

fields.doc: Lattice cells per pixel (feTurbulence `baseFrequency`): 0.8 a fine grain, 0.05 soft clouds.
Octaves summed, each twice the frequency at half the amplitude.
The random seed: the same seed draws the same grain.
`fractalNoise` (a soft grain) or `turbulence` (ridged).

Pagination.doc: A pagination controller: loads a list's items page by page and exposes its state as a map variable named `name` (`${name.items}`, `${name.page}`, `${name.pageCount}`, `${name.hasMore}`, `${name.isLoadingMore}`, `${name.error}`...). Paginate actions move it.

fields.doc: The map variable that holds the state, unique on its page.
The page sizes a pagination node offers; empty offers none.
The path in an item of the value that identifies it; items with the same value show once. Empty keeps every item.
The page shown first, from 1.
How many items from the end (or start) the next page starts loading.
The same in pixels of scroll left; 0 uses `thresholdItems` alone.
Loaded pages are kept to show again until a refresh.
The API (`PaginationSource.api`).
The API call's parameters (`${page.page}`...).
Where in an API response the page's items, the total count and the next cursor are (empty: the response itself, unknown, none).
Pull to refresh (`RefreshIndicator`): the list's `refresh` reactions.

Paint.doc: A fill or stroke paint: a solid color, a gradient or an image. Several paints stack, first at the bottom.

fields.doc: What the paint is: `solid` (a colour), `linear`, `radial`, `sweep` or `diamond` (a gradient of `stops`), `image`, or `noise`. Without one: an image if it has `image`, a linear gradient if it has `stops`, else solid.
Stable id, so a binding can target one paint (`fill-<id>`).
False keeps the paint but does not draw it.
The paint's opacity, 0 to 1, multiplied with its colours' own alpha.
How the paint blends with what is under it (CSS `mix-blend-mode`).
Solid color (type `solid`).
Gradient stops (gradient types).

Six numbers `[a, b, tx, c, d, ty]` mapping a point (x, y) of the box, in its unit square (0 to 1 each way), into the gradient's unit square: u = a·x + b·y + tx, v = c·x + d·y + ty. A linear gradient runs along u from 0 to 1; `[20, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]` with `"tileMode": "repeated"` repeats it 20 times across the box. Simpler: `begin`/`end` (linear) or `center`/`radius` (radial).
Linear: where the gradient starts, an alignment (`[-1, 0]` or `"centerLeft"`, Flutter `LinearGradient.begin`). Read into `transform`; default the left edge.

Linear: where the gradient ends (Flutter `LinearGradient.end`). `"begin": [0, -1], "end": [0, 1]` runs top to bottom; `"begin": [-1, 0], "end": [-0.9, 0]` with `"tileMode": "repeated"` repeats it every 5% of the width.
Radial: its center, an alignment (`[0, -1]`: the middle of the top edge; Flutter `RadialGradient.center`). Read into `transform`; default the box's center.
What a gradient does past `begin` and `end`: `clamp` (keeps the end colours), `repeated`, `mirror`, `decal`.
Image (type `image`).

Radial: the radius as a share of the box's shortest side (Flutter's RadialGradient); null: half the box's width (as the transform maps it). Past the last stop the gradient keeps the last stop's color (`tileMode` clamp): end a glow on a transparent stop, or it fills the rest of the box.

A gradient's length in logical pixels, whatever the box's size: linear, from `begin` toward `end` (only their direction counts then); radial, its radius. With `"tileMode": "repeated"` the stops repeat every `length` px: CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, #1F2937 0 1px, transparent 1px 80px)` is `{"type": "linear", "begin": "topCenter", "end": "bottomCenter", "length": 80, "tileMode": "repeated", "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FF1F2937"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#FF1F2937"}, {"position": 0.0125, "color": "#00000000"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#00000000"}]}`: a 1 px line every 80 px (a background grid is two such paints).

Type `noise`: procedural grain, as SVG `<feTurbulence>`: `{"baseFrequency": 0.8, "numOctaves": 3, "seed": 0, "type": "fractalNoise"}`. With `color` the grain is that color, its alpha the noise; without, the four noise channels feTurbulence gives. Fade it with `opacity` (a film grain: 0.05 to 0.12) and set a `blendMode` (`overlay`, `softLight`) as CSS `mix-blend-mode`. Drawn as a seamless 256 px tile repeated over the box.

Pan.doc:
Follows the pointer (node key `pan`): `GestureDetector(onPanUpdate:)` moving a `Transform.translate`. On release it springs back to rest or stays (`release`), with `physics` a fling that slows by friction, a spring and snap points within `bounds` and the limits `minX`...`maxY` (a bottom sheet: `{"axis": "vertical", "release": "stay", "minY": -560, "maxY": 0, "physics": {"snap": {"points": [[0, 0], [0, -560]]}}}`). Its offset binds two-way to `xVariable` and `yVariable`; `x` and `y` (bindable) place its rest.

Inside it `${pan.dx}`, `${pan.dy}`, `${pan.dragging}`, `${pan.settling}`, `${pan.snapIndex}` can be read (and the same as `${drag.*}`). It fires `drag` and `dragEnd`.

fields.doc: Bindable as `pan.enabled`.
The axis it moves on (`Draggable.axis`, `InteractiveViewer.panAxis`).
The spring back without physics.
Its rest, from its layout's place (pixels).
Where it rests, from where its layout puts it (pixels; bindable as `pan.x`, `pan.y`): it springs back here, and a new value moves it.
Number variables its offset from where its layout puts it is written to (rounded to hundredths) as it moves.
Number variables its offset from where its layout puts it is written to (rounded to hundredths) as it moves.
The release's fling, spring and snap points.
What it's kept inside of while dragged and flung, narrowed by the offsets from rest `minX`...`maxY` (null: no limit).
Offsets from rest it stays within (pixels; null no limit).

ParticleEmitter.doc:
Confetti, stars or emoji the node bursts with on cue.

Each particle leaves from the origin at `speed` (55–115%) in a direction within `spread` of `direction`, slows by `drag`, falls by `gravity` no faster than `terminalVelocity`, sways `sway` px side to side, spins and turns over (`flutter`), and fades out over the last `fadeOut` ms of its `lifetime`.

fields.doc: Over how long the particles leave (0: all at once).
Degrees.
Wait after the cue (ms).
Speed lost per second, e^(-drag).
The fastest fall (px/s; 0: no limit).
Side-to-side sway (px).
Turning over in 3D (radians per second, up to).
Spin (degrees per second, up to).
Fade out over the end of each particle's life (ms).
Two cannons: every other particle mirrored across the middle.
The text emoji particles draw.
The image `image` particles draw (a URL).

PathFollow.doc:
A place along an SVG path: `progress` (0–1) of the way along `path`'s length, turned with it as `orient` says. Shared by `motion.path` and a drag track's path.

Values of `progress` outside 0–1 wrap round a closed path (one that ends where it starts) and clamp to the ends of an open one.

JSON: `{"path": "M0 0 C 40 -60, 120 -60, 160 0", "progress": 0.5, "orient": "tangent"}`; a bare string reads as `path`.

fields.doc: SVG path data.
The path's coordinate space `[width, height]`, stretched over the node's parent; empty: pixels from the node's place.
0–1 of its length; wraps on a closed path.

PlotChartLabel.doc: A label on a plot chart's x axis, centered on `x`.

PlotChartMarker.doc: A labeled dot on a plot chart (on the curve when `y` is null).

fields.doc: The marker's shape. A ring and a square are outlined in `color` and filled with `fillColor`; a dot is filled with `color`; a diamond is filled with `fillColor` and outlined in `strokeColor`.
The size: a dot's or ring's radius, half a square's side, a diamond's half diagonal. Null uses the chart's markerRadius.
An outline around a dot or diamond (none by default for a dot; black for a diamond).
The outline width (default 2 for a ring and square, 1.2 for a dot or diamond's `strokeColor`).

PlotChartRange.doc: A shaded x range of a plot chart, painted behind the curve.

PlotChartSeries.doc: One more curve on a plot chart, over the chart's x domain: `points` are evenly spaced from xMin to xMax like the chart's own, and a null point is a gap (the line breaks there: an undefined value or an asymptote).

PlotChartYLine.doc: A horizontal line across a plot chart at `y`: a grid line, or a reference such as a target (dashed, with an inline `label`). `axisLabel` is written in the chart's y-axis gutter (`PlotChartProps.yAxisWidth`).

Pose.doc: A `Motion` drawn with a fade and a blur: the pose a page of a page view (`pageMotion`) or a side of a route transition is drawn at. Flutter: a `Transform` in an `Opacity` in an `ImageFiltered`. JSON: `motion`'s keys with `opacity` and `blur` beside them, flat (`{"shiftX": -1, "opacity": 0.5}`).

fields.doc: Pixels.
Pixels (`Transform.translate(offset:)`).
Times the node's size (`FractionalTranslation`).
Multiples of the node's own size (`FractionalTranslation`).
The axis factors multiply `scale`.
`Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`.
`Transform.scale(scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:)`: the axis factors multiply `scale`.
Degrees, about z.
Degrees, in 3D.
Degrees. `rotate` turns about z (`Transform.rotate`); `rotateX` and `rotateY` turn in 3D, seen with `perspective` (0 flat).
How strongly a 3D rotation is seen in depth (0 flat).
Not painted while its back faces the viewer (through every transform above it too).
A layer blur's radius.

ProgressBand.doc: A colored zone of an arc progress bar, from `start` to `end` as fractions of the max value.

RadioGroupBehavior.doc: Flutter's `RadioGroup`: the `radio` nodes inside the node that set no `groupValue` of their own share this one, and choosing one of them runs the node's `changed` reactions with its value as `${result}` (`RadioGroup.onChanged`). Bind `groupValue` to the variable the choice is kept in: `"bind": {"radioGroup.groupValue": "${budget}"}`.

fields.doc: The value of the radio that is on; bind it to the variable the choice is kept in.

Reveal.doc: Scrolls the node into view when it appears (or when its `reveal.when` binding turns true), to `alignment` of the viewport (0 top, 1 bottom). With `follow` it stays there while the content around it moves (lines added above an end marker, an image that loads late), until the user scrolls away: a chat or transcript pinned to its newest line.

fields.doc: Where in the viewport (0 top, 1 bottom).
Stays revealed while the content moves, until the user scrolls away.

RouteDismiss.doc: A drag anywhere on a screen that closes it interactively: the drag runs the transition backwards, and on release the pop completes or cancels with `spring`.

fields.doc: The way the screen is dragged to close it.
The share of the screen's size along `direction` a slow drag must pass.
A fling faster than this (px/s) toward `direction` closes it.

RouteTransition.doc: A composable route transition. `enter` is where the incoming screen starts, `exit` where the covered one ends; closing plays them in reverse unless `popEnter` (where the screen revealed by the pop starts) or `popExit` (where the closing screen goes) are given. A `preset` fills in what's left null. JSON: an object, or a bare preset name.

fields.doc: A ready-made transition; the sides given override its own.
Where the incoming screen starts.
Where the covered screen ends.
Null: exit reversed.
Null: enter reversed.
Null: the preset's (300).
Null: `durationMs`.
Drawn behind a modal (or a see-through page) while it's open. Null: none on pages, the dialog's own on modals.
Whether the screen hides the one below once open. Null: the preset's (true without one).
Null: the preset's (`RouteSwipeBack.platform` without one).
A drag that closes the screen.

ShapeBorder.doc: One of Flutter's `OutlinedBorder`s: its kind, corner radius and side. JSON: `{"type": "stadium", "borderRadius": 8, "side": {...}}`.

fields.doc: Corner radii (rectangle types).
The outline; null draws none.

Shimmer.doc: A band of light across what the node paints (a loading skeleton's shimmer: Flutter's `ShaderMask` with a moving `LinearGradient`), blended over the node's own pixels only. `position` places it; the `shimmer` animation preset sweeps it across, over and over. JSON (sparse): `{"color": "#FFFFFFFF", "strength": 0.8, "width": 0.44, "angle": 0, "position": 0.5}`.

fields.doc: How strongly the band's center blends the color in (0–1).
A share of the node's size along the sweep.
Degrees: 0 left to right, 90 top to bottom.
0 off the start side, 1 off the end (the `shimmer` preset sweeps it).

Spring.doc: Flutter's `SpringDescription`: either the physical triple (`SpringDescription(mass:, stiffness:, damping:)`, when `stiffness` and `damping` are both given) or `SpringDescription.withDurationAndBounce` (`duration` ms, `bounce`). The one spring value of the model: transitions, animations, gestures, a flip card's settle and a route's dismiss all take it. JSON: `{"stiffness": 380, "damping": 36}` or `{"duration": 500, "bounce": 0.3}` (sparse; `{}` is `withDurationAndBounce()`'s defaults).

fields.doc: The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`.
The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`.
`withDurationAndBounce`: ms, and 0 (none) to 1.

StateStyles.doc: What a node and its descendants change to in each `WidgetState`: per state, node id → a patch of that node's JSON (a merge patch: maps merge, `null` removes, anything else replaces; see `mergePatch`). Later states in `WidgetState`'s order win where active states overlap.

Sticky.doc: Pins the node inside the scrolling row or column it scrolls in, as CSS `position: sticky`: once its leading edge reaches `offset` from the view's leading edge it stays there, drawn above the content scrolling under it, until the end of its parent (the section it heads) pushes it on. `${sticky.stuck}` says whether it is pinned now (the node's own bindings and the nodes inside it read it). The design canvas, which doesn't scroll, draws it in place. JSON `true` or `{"offset": 8}`.

fields.doc: Distance from the view's leading edge where it pins (px).

SwipeAction.doc: One action revealed behind a list item as it is swiped.

fields.doc: The action in `${result.action}`.
Takes the item out of the list (delete, archive); otherwise it springs back.
Offered for an item only while this holds (an expression reading `${item}`, e.g. `${= item.done}`); empty: always. The first action of a side that holds is the one a full swipe runs.
The label's text (font, size, weight; its color is `foreground`).
The icon beside the label instead of above it.

SwipeActions.doc: Swipe actions on a list's items (`Dismissible`): toward the start reveals `endActions`, toward the end `startActions`; past `threshold` the first of the side runs. Running one fires the list's `swipeAction` reactions with `${result.action}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.index}`.

fields.doc: The fraction of the item's width a swipe passes to run the first action.
An action that removes the item shows an Undo bar first.
`${result.label}` reads the action's label.
The revealed actions' corners (round them to match the item's).
The action's label grows to this scale once a release would run it.
A selection click when a swipe passes the threshold either way.

TableColumn.doc: One column of a table view: the row field its cells show (`key`, read as `${item.value}`), its header text (`label`, `${item.label}`) and its width (null: the table's `columnWidth`).

fields.doc: The column's share of the room left when the table is wider than its columns (its width is then the least it takes); 0: fixed.

TextRun.doc: A styled range of a text's characters, `[start, end)`.

fields.doc: A URL the run opens when tapped.

TextStyle.doc: Flutter's `TextStyle`. Every field is optional: a span's style is merged over its text's base style, as in `Text.rich`.

The font family (`"Inter"`); `fontWeight` picks its file. Without one: the platform's default (Roboto).
Flutter's `FontWeight`: 100–900, in hundreds.
`normal` or `italic`.
The font size in logical pixels. Without one: 12.
Solid text color.
A gradient or image paint for the glyphs, used instead of `color`.
Logical pixels between letters.
Line height as a multiple of the font size. Unset: the inherited defaultTextStyle's, else the font's own (Flutter's height: null, CSS line-height: normal).
A line through the text: `underline`, `overline`, `lineThrough` or `none`.
The colour of the `decoration` line; without one, the text's colour.
Painted behind the glyphs.
The `decoration` line's style: `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `wavy`.
The `decoration` line's thickness, as a multiple of the font's default.
Fixed-width digits (`OpenTypeFeature.tabularFigures`).
OpenType feature settings (`"lnum"`, `"ss01"`, `"liga=0"`).

A key on a node that is neither a node field nor a behavior: it is kept but does nothing.
A key in "props" that the node type does not declare: it does nothing.
A key in "layout" that layout does not read.
A key in "decoration" that decoration does not read.
A key inside a value (a paint, a text style, a behavior model...) that its type does not read.
A value of the wrong JSON type or shape: decoding ignores it and uses the default.
A value of another JSON type that decoding converts (the text "12" for a number): write the type itself.
A value that is not one of the allowed names: decoding uses the default.
A number outside its declared bounds: decoding clamps it.
Fills, strokes, radius or shadows on a type without a box decoration: only blur effects are kept.
A child id that names no node.
A slot whose id names no node.
A node listed as a child (or slot) of more than one parent, or twice in one parent.
A node that contains itself.
A node no root reaches: it is never shown.
A slot name the node type does not have.
A "children" list on a type that takes none (or takes slots only): they are never shown.
A "slots" map on a type that has no slots.
A canvas used as the child of another node: canvases are screens, only roots.
A layout field the node's parent does not read (x/y outside a stack, flex/align outside a row or column).
A width or height mode the parent cannot honor (fill along a scrolling axis, flexible outside a row/column).
A fixed width or height of 0 (often a missing "width"/"height"): the node is invisible.
A wrapping list that scrolls vertically: its items flow top to bottom and wrap into columns, not side by side.
A layout value that cannot take effect as written: a negative offset in a stack that hugs its children (clamped to 0), or a negative margin (Flutter has none: the box shrinks).
A prop that has no effect with another the node sets (a grid's mainAxisExtent while shrinkWrapRows sizes its rows): one of them is ignored.
A bound "selected" with no "states.selected" style: the node is selected, but nothing changes how it looks.
A "bind" key that names no bindable field of the node.
A binding path that is kept but not applied yet.
A "${" that is not closed, or an empty ${}.
An expression reads a name that is neither a declared variable nor a scope the runtime provides.
A reaction whose trigger type is unknown or missing: the reaction is dropped.
A key of a trigger that triggers do not read.
An action type no declaration knows: the runtime skips it.
A key of an action that its type does not read.
An action or condition names a node id that is not in the document.
A navigate or openModal names a screen (canvas or layout id) that does not exist.
An action or trigger names a variable that is not declared.
A reaction or action that is not an object, or an action list that is not a list.
A variable without a name, with an unknown type, or whose value its type cannot hold.
Two variables of the same name in one scope.
Variables or conditions keyed by an id that is not a canvas of the document (nor page_variables).
A condition, branch, predicate or set entry of the wrong shape.
A canvas, variant or media rule names a breakpoint the project does not define.

A "media" rule of the wrong shape: no condition (minWidth, maxWidth, orientation), a width that is neither px nor a breakpoint name, a minWidth above its maxWidth, or a patch key that cannot vary by screen size.
A media rule patches a field the node also binds: the binding wins, so the patch never shows.
A color or text style names a color or text style the project's theme (the site manifest's "theme") does not have: it would show transparent or unstyled.
The site manifest's "theme" is not of the right shape: colors are "#AARRGGBB" (or another color's name), text styles are TextStyle objects, media rules patch colors and textStyles.

A colour role (primary, onPrimary, surface, onSurface, error, success, warning: Flutter's ColorScheme names) written inside the theme's "colors": roles are top-level keys of the theme, so controls never read it. Move it up ("primary": "#FF..." or "primary": "<a colour's name>").
The site manifest's "fonts" is not of the right shape: a list of {"family": "Inter", "fonts": [{"asset": "fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", "weight": 400, "style": "normal"}]} (a pubspec's fonts: section).
A declared font file is not .ttf, .otf or .woff: WOFF2 (Brotli-compressed) and font collections (.ttc) are not read. Use the .woff or .ttf of the same face.
Two canvases of one screen are the design for the same breakpoint.
A canvas grouped into a screen (props.screen) that names no breakpoint: it shows only below the narrowest.
The same canvas id in two documents of one project: navigate and openModal name a screen by its canvas id, so a link reaches one of them. Other node ids are per document and may repeat.
A call names a component type (UpperCamelCase) that no definition of the project declares: it renders as an empty box of its size.
Two definitions declare the same component type, or a component type is also a catalog type: there is no shadowing.
A component calls itself, directly or through other components: it can never finish rendering.
A component document whose file name (or "id") is not its widget type: a file holds the component it is named after.
A component document of the wrong shape: a "widget" without a type, a type that is not UpperCamelCase, or not exactly one root.
A call does not set a parameter the component declares as required.
An event reaction (or a componentEvent action) names an event the component does not declare, or sits on a node that is not a component call.
A field on a call that belongs to the definition (decoration, layout.padding): the call gives size and placement only.
A slot node in a document that is not a component: nothing fills it, its own children show.
A component root binds its size or placement: the call sizes and places the root, so the binding is dropped.
A subtree written several times over, node for node (ids and names aside): a component, or a list template, would write it once.
